steps.title: 1 · The Skeleton
steps.body: 206 bones make up the adult skeleton. It's split into two groups: the axial skeleton (skull, spine, ribs, sternum) running down the body's centerline, and the appendicular skeleton — the arms, legs, and the girdles that attach them.

steps.title: 2 · Skull — protecting the brain
steps.body: Many separate bones (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, and more) fuse together at rigid joints called sutures to form a single protective case around the brain.

steps.title: 3 · Mandible — the only moving skull bone
steps.body: Every other skull bone is fused in place. The mandible is the exception — it hinges at a joint in front of each ear, letting you open, close, and grind your jaw.

steps.title: 4 · Cervical Vertebrae — the neck
steps.body: Seven small vertebrae (C1–C7) support the skull. The top two are specially shaped to let your head nod (C1, the atlas) and rotate (C2, the axis).

steps.title: 5 · Thoracic Vertebrae — anchoring the ribs
steps.body: Twelve vertebrae (T1–T12), each with a facet where a pair of ribs attaches. This is what turns the spine and ribs into one connected cage.

steps.title: 6 · Ribs — the protective cage
steps.body: Twelve pairs curve from the spine around to the front of the chest, shielding the heart and lungs while still flexing outward with every breath.

steps.title: 7 · Sternum — closing the cage
steps.body: The breastbone, in the center of the chest. Most ribs attach here via cartilage, completing the rib cage's protective enclosure.

steps.title: 8 · Lumbar Vertebrae — the lower back
steps.body: Five large, sturdy vertebrae (L1–L5) built to bear most of your upper body's weight — and the most common site of lower-back strain.

steps.title: 9 · Hip Bone — spine meets legs
steps.body: The sacrum wedges between the two hip bones to form the pelvis, transferring your body's weight from the spine down into the legs.

steps.title: 10 · Femur — the body's longest bone
steps.body: The thigh bone. Its rounded head fits into the hip socket, and its lower end forms the knee — a single bone doing the work of an entire leg's main support.

steps.title: 11 · Tibia — carrying your weight
steps.body: The shin bone carries nearly all your weight below the knee. Its thinner neighbor, the fibula, mostly just stabilizes the ankle.

steps.title: 12 · Humerus — the upper arm
steps.body: The single bone of the upper arm. Its rounded head sits in the scapula's shallow socket — a loose fit that trades stability for the shoulder's huge range of motion.

steps.title: 13 · Bones of the Hand
steps.body: 27 small bones in each hand — 8 carpals in the wrist, 5 metacarpals in the palm, and 14 phalanges in the fingers — giving your hand the fine control no other body part has.

steps.title: 14 · Bones of the Foot
steps.body: 26 bones per foot, arranged into arches that absorb the shock of every step — including the calcaneus, your heel bone, and the talus, which forms the ankle joint.
